cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a carved wooden Belum figure set — malevolent spirit figures (tew), paddle, stone, and stand — made of sago palm pith, a well-documented Melanau ritual/healing tradition from Sarawak. This is a positive match for Melanau material culture.

physical.title: stand; figure; paddle
physical.summary: Belum (image of a tew, i.e., malevolent spirit) (part of set with five figures, stand, paddle and shell); carved of sago palm pith; a) part of stand: piece of wood, carved to point at one end, opposite end with mortise slot cut; hole carved at pointed end with spike inserted into it; three holes carved along top to support figures; hole carved in mortise slot to fit spike to fasten second piece of stand; b) part of stand: piece of wood with mortise slot carved in each end; hole carved through each mortise slot, with wooden spike inserted into one to fasten to second part of stand; two pairs of holes carved to support figures; c) and g) male human figure: thin flat human figure, head-dress with diamond-shaped hole carved at centre, outside edges serrated, arms bent and hands held up to chest, spikes along back, spiked dowel inserted in hole in bottom of figure to mount on stand; d)-e) male human figure: thin flat human figure, head-dress with two diamond-shaped holes carved, outside edges serrated, arms bent and hands held up to chest, spikes along back, spiked dowel inserted in hole in bottom of figure to mount on stand; f) male human figure: thin flat human figure, head-dress with outside edges serrated, arms bent and hands held up to chest, spikes along back, spiked dowel inserted in hole in bottom of figure to mount on stand; h) paddle: rectangular piece of wood with one long side carved into curve; hole carved on either end; i) shell: circular portion of coconut shell; together represents the water spirit Bilum Bela'ud.
